The SMART for TBI Act (H.R. 1493) reauthorizes surveillance programs and pushes AI integration for traumatic brain injury care—a critical focus given that 82% of military TBIs are classified as mild yet often lead to chronic cognitive issues. While the bill's emphasis on digital health tools aligns with the Pentagon's Warfighter Brain Health Initiative, we must scrutinize whether this $55 million reauthorization duplicates existing efforts like the Joint Autonomy Office's work on adaptive neurotechnologies.

The cited study from Frontiers in Neurology (2025) shows Strategic Memory Advanced Reasoning Training (SMART) already achieves 60% cost savings over traditional therapies through shorter treatment durations. Rather than layering new bureaucracy, we should optimize proven programs and redirect savings to frontline care.

Military medical spending must prioritize battlefield-ready solutions over redundant systems—every dollar should enhance cognitive lethality, not fund D.C. middlemen.
